turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first; I'd like to know who decided that, and on what basis.
Can I ask something off the record?
Nothing in this room is off the record, Hale. I'm writing down everything you say. Who decided on the zero?
When was the last time you actually sat with him while he did homework?
My parenting isn't what's on trial here, Hale. You entered a zero before anyone called me, and you still haven't told me on what basis. Answer that.
Because in my experience, kids who cheat have parents who are too busy to notice.

"Kids who cheat have parents who are too busy to notice." I'm writing that down word for word, Hale, and I'll be reading it to the principal before I leave this building. My son didn't cheat, so unless you have something with a date on it, we're done with your experience.
